idiom_name: type-tag enum plus translator function-pointer table into one canonical struct
implementation_notes: C has no standard serialization layer, so the normalizer is the classic structure written out: one parse function per source format, a single canonical struct that is the only type downstream sees, and a table of {detector, translator} function-pointer pairs that the routing step walks - the callback-table dispatch style the C standard library itself uses for qsort's comparator. Detection is entirely hand-rolled (file name or extension, first-line sniffing, field count, a fixed offset marker) because C has no reflective type information, and the canonical struct must be filled by an explicit mapping function that also applies unit, date and code conversions. The classic form is always the right one here; the only real choices are a static table versus a switch on the tag enum, and whether translators allocate into an arena or write directly into a caller-provided struct.
pitfalls: String handling is the trap: strcpy/sprintf into fixed-size canonical fields, missing NUL terminators and strtok's global state (not thread-safe - use strtok_r or a hand-written scanner) are the usual memory-safety failures at this seam.

Ownership of parsed strings has to be decided once: if every translator allocates into the canonical struct, the caller needs a matching canonical_msg_free and every early error path must free what was already built.

Detection and translation are two passes over the same bytes, so an unbounded sniff (strlen on untrusted input, reading past len) recreates a read-overrun attack surface before the message is even validated.
